sub_areas.name: Downtown Brampton (Four Corners)
sub_areas.note: Historic city centre at Queen and Main Streets in the southwest part of the city (Wikipedia). OGS point queries at the reference coordinate and at Brampton GO Station (43.68694, -79.76472) both return clay-to-silt till (unit 5d) over Queenston Formation shale.

sub_areas.name: Bramalea
sub_areas.note: Large planned 'new town' district east of the original town, in former Chinguacousy Township, developed from the 1960s by Bramalea Limited (Wikipedia). OGS point queries at the Wikipedia article coordinate (43.725, -79.7175) and at Bramalea City Centre (43.716589, -79.723921) return unit 5d till over Georgian Bay Formation; at Bramalea GO Station (43.70194, -79.69111) the surficial unit changes to fine-textured glaciolacustrine silt and clay (unit 8b).

sub_areas.name: Heart Lake
sub_areas.note: North-central Brampton around Heart Lake Conservation Area (169 ha, Etobicoke Creek watershed, TRCA-managed; the TRCA describes its surficial geology as glacial till and river deposits, per Wikipedia). OGS point query at the conservation area (43.742, -79.795) returns unit 5d till over Queenston Formation. The residential neighbourhood south of the park was not separately queried.

sub_areas.name: Springdale
sub_areas.note: Suburban district of about 1,600 ha in the north of the city, bounded by Countryside Drive, Bovaird Drive, Heart Lake Road and Airport Road (Wikipedia). OGS point query at the OpenStreetMap neighbourhood node (43.7539, -79.7695) returns unit 5d till over Queenston Formation.

sub_areas.name: Castlemore
sub_areas.note: Northeast Brampton, about 14 km from downtown, developed since the early 1990s with some 2-acre estate lots; the West Humber River flows through its western portion (Wikipedia). OGS point query at the Wikipedia coordinate (43.79095, -79.6897) returns fine-textured glaciolacustrine silt and clay (unit 8b) over Georgian Bay Formation.

sub_areas.name: Mount Pleasant
sub_areas.note: Northwest Brampton, a former rural hamlet that has grown rapidly since Mount Pleasant GO Station opened in 2005 (Wikipedia). OGS point query at the Wikipedia coordinate (43.67667, -79.81861) returns unit 5d till over Queenston Formation.

sub_areas.name: Churchville
sub_areas.note: Preserved hamlet in southwest Brampton on the Credit River, designated a heritage conservation district in 1990, the city's only one (Wikipedia). OGS point query at the Wikipedia coordinate (43.63, -79.75556) returns coarse-textured glaciolacustrine sand and gravel (unit 9c, foreshore and basinal deposits) over Queenston Formation, the only coarse-textured surficial unit found at any Brampton query point.

sub_areas.name: Snelgrove
sub_areas.note: Former hamlet in the northwest of the city (Wikipedia coordinate 43.73389, -79.82444). OGS point query returns unit 5d till over Queenston Formation. Included only as an additional geology sample point.

surficial.description: Clay to silt-textured till (derived from glaciolacustrine deposits or shale). This is the unit regional literature calls Halton Till / the Peel Plain, but those names are not carried in the OGS layer attributes and were not verified here.
surficial.where: Nearly all of Brampton: query points at the reference coordinate, Brampton GO Station (downtown), Bramalea (Wikipedia coordinate and Bramalea City Centre), Heart Lake Conservation Area, Springdale, Mount Pleasant and Snelgrove all return unit 5d (one continuous polygon, OBJECTID 89680).

surficial.unit: OGS MRD128-REV unit 8b - Fine-textured glaciolacustrine deposits
surficial.description: Silt and clay, minor sand and gravel; interbedded silt and clay and gritty, pebbly flow till and rainout deposits.
surficial.where: East and northeast Brampton: query points at Bramalea GO Station (Steeles Ave E and Bramalea Rd, 43.70194, -79.69111) and Castlemore (43.79095, -79.6897) return unit 8b.

surficial.unit: OGS MRD128-REV unit 9c - Coarse-textured glaciolacustrine deposits
surficial.description: Sand, gravel, minor silt and clay; foreshore and basinal deposits.
surficial.where: Churchville, on the Credit River in southwest Brampton (query point 43.63, -79.75556).

bedrock.formation: Queenston Formation (west and central Brampton, including downtown) and Georgian Bay Formation (east Brampton, Bramalea and Castlemore); both Upper Ordovician shale-dominated units (OGS MRD219, source map m2337).
bedrock.description: Queenston (OGS unit 16): red shale and siltstone, minor green shale and siltstone, and variable calcareous siltstone to sandstone and limestone interbeds. Georgian Bay (OGS unit 14): interbedded grey-green to dark grey shale and fossiliferous calcareous siltstone to bioclastic limestone. OGS point queries return Queenston at the reference coordinate, Brampton GO, Heart Lake, Springdale, Mount Pleasant, Churchville and Snelgrove, and Georgian Bay at Bramalea (both points), Bramalea GO and Castlemore; the contact runs roughly north-south between downtown and Bramalea.
bedrock.depth_note: Depth to bedrock was not retrieved (no drift-thickness dataset queried). No Brampton query point returned OGS unit 3 (bedrock at or near surface), so shallow shale was not indicated at any of the eleven points sampled; the City's own deck drawings list 'clay shale' (300 kPa) and 'till' (200 kPa) among the soil types a builder may encounter, but give no depths.

implications_for_piles: The City of Brampton's deck permit package sets the baseline any pile design is compared against: concrete piers 8, 10 or 12 inches in diameter a minimum of 4'-0" below grade, bearing on undisturbed soil, with the soil bearing capacity to be determined prior to construction (General Note 7). The package does not mention helical piles, CCMC or BMEC evaluations, or an engineer requirement for alternative foundations; the drawings simply ask the applicant to provide the location, depth, size and spacing of piers.

The same drawings print a soil bearing table (soft clay 40 kPa, loose sand or gravel 50, firm clay 75, dense or compact silt 100, stiff clay 150, dense compact sand or gravel 150, till 200, clay shale 300, sound rock 500 kPa) and require the allowable bearing pressure to be reduced by 50% where water is at or near the bottom of the footing excavation (General Note 10).

OGS surficial mapping is unusually uniform across Brampton: eight of eleven query points fall in one clay-to-silt till polygon (unit 5d). The exceptions are the east side (Bramalea GO, Castlemore), where fine-textured glaciolacustrine silt and clay (unit 8b) is mapped, and Churchville on the Credit River, where coarse sand and gravel (unit 9c) is mapped; pile depth and torque expectations from the till plain are therefore not transferable to those areas.

Bedrock is Queenston red shale under the west and centre and Georgian Bay grey shale under the east; no query point showed bedrock at or near surface, and depth to bedrock is not known from the sources retrieved. No site-specific depth, torque or capacity figures were retrieved.

permits.authority: City of Brampton Building Division (the City's pages refer to 'the Building Division's Permits Section' and to 'Building Services' for inspection booking; located at Flower City Community Campus, 8850 McLaughlin Road South, Unit 1)
permits.deck_permit_required_when: A building permit is required for any deck or porch that is physically attached or anchored to the house, and for any deck or porch that is 0.6 metres or more above the ground. A deck, porch or patio less than 0.6 metres (2 feet) above the ground and not attached to the house is permitted by the Zoning By-law and does not require a building permit. The deck must also meet Zoning By-law setbacks and permitted encroachments; if the property is in an area regulated by Credit Valley Conservation or the Toronto and Region Conservation Authority, that authority's approval is needed before the City can issue the permit.
permits.footing_depth_requirement: City deck package drawings (Deck Foundation Plan and Deck Sections, revised Feb 2026): concrete piers 8", 10" or 12" diameter 'MINIMUM 4'-0" BELOW GRADE'; General Note 7: 'CONCRETE PIERS SHALL BEAR ON UNDISTURBED SOIL. THE BEARING CAPACITY OF THE SOIL SHALL BE DETERMINED PRIOR TO CONSTRUCTION'; General Note 10: allowable soil bearing pressure reduced by 50% while water is at or near the bottom of the footing excavation. The application checklist asks for 'location, depth, size and spacing of piers'. The package makes no mention of helical piles, CCMC or BMEC evaluations, or engineer requirements for alternative foundations.
permits.fee_note: 2026 Fee Schedule (revised February 2026): Deck, flat fee $326.21, the same as the minimum fee for detached, semi-detached, townhouse, rowhouse, duplex or live/work residential projects; the deck package states 'Permit fee of $326.21 applies to our Standard 10 Day Permit Application Service'.
permits.timeline_note: The City's Standard Permit Application Service covers all home renovation projects and 'the Building Division will provide a review of your application within 10 business days'. Inspections run 8 am to 4 pm Monday to Friday, can be booked up to 5 days in advance, and the next business day closes for booking at 3 pm each day; the mandatory inspections for decks are to be requested in the order Footing, Structural Framing, Final.
permits.portal_note: Applications, inspection bookings and document requests go through the Brampton Building & Business Portal (registered user, or guest with permit number and authorization key for inspections); the paper 'Permit to Construct or Demolish' form is no longer required because it is part of the portal submission.

climate.station: Toronto Pearson International Airport (Climate ID 6158731, WMO 71624; 43 40'36" N, 79 37'50" W; 173.4 m), about 11 km southeast of the Brampton reference coordinate. No ECCC normals station named Brampton exists in the 1981-2010 or 1991-2020 search.
climate.normals_period: 1991-2020 (temperature code B, 30 years; day-count and frost tables code C; record combines 6158733 to 2013/06/13 and 6158731 thereafter)
climate.freeze_thaw_note: Toronto Pearson 1991-2020: January daily minimum -8.9 C; average last spring frost Apr 27, first fall frost Oct 20; 130.6 days/yr with minimum <= 0 C versus 49.5 days/yr with maximum <= 0 C, so roughly 81 days a year cross 0 C between night and day (derived by subtraction); 101.0 days/yr below -2 C; 2.7 days/yr below -20 C; 114.5 cm annual snowfall. Brampton's reference point is 11 km northwest of and slightly higher than the airport, so winters are unlikely to be milder than these figures.
